subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should denied non-owner, unknown-sender, and ambient room-event turns continue seeing the four protected core-tool schemas when every call is blocked before hooks and side effects?
rationale: Source inspection verifies layered enforcement, but only maintainers can decide whether protected-schema disclosure is an acceptable permanent tradeoff for prompt-cache stability.

options.title: Approve stable schemas
options.body: Keep the stable catalogue and require immutable turn policy with denial before hooks, implementations, and side effects across native and loopback paths.

options.title: Keep schemas hidden
options.body: Retain prompt-time filtering and redesign cache stability without disclosing protected tool definitions to denied turns.

recommendation.title: Approve stable schemas
recommendation.body: Keep the stable catalogue and require immutable turn policy with denial before hooks, implementations, and side effects across native and loopback paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Major Codex lifecycle and MCP loopback refactors make this the strongest available owner for coordinating the cross-cutting security-boundary decision.
